name: Mephibosheth
title: Jonathan's Lame Son
summary: Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul. He became lame in both feet after a fall as a child when news of Saul’s and Jonathan’s death reached them. King David showed him kindness for Jonathan’s sake and let him eat at the king’s table for the rest of his life.

keyEvents.title: The Fall as a Child
keyEvents.description: When Mephibosheth was five years old, his nurse fled with him after hearing the news of Saul and Jonathan’s death. She fell with the child in her arms, and he became lame in both feet.

keyEvents.title: David Seeks Out Saul's Descendants
keyEvents.description: David looked for someone from Saul’s household to show kindness to for Jonathan’s sake. His servant Ziba told him about Mephibosheth, who was living in Lo-debar.

keyEvents.title: David shows kindness and gives him a place at the king's table
keyEvents.description: David called Mefibosjet to himself, returned all of Saul's land to him, and let him eat at the king's table as one of the king's own sons. Ziba and his household were assigned to work the land for him.

keyEvents.title: Ziba's betrayal during Absalom's rebellion
keyEvents.description: During Absalom's rebellion, Ziba met David with gifts and claimed that Mefibosjet had stayed behind in Jerusalem to regain Saul's throne. David then gave Ziba everything that belonged to Mefibosjet.

keyEvents.title: Mefibosjet's defense after David's return
keyEvents.description: When David returned to Jerusalem, Mefibosjet met him in mourning and explained that Ziba had deceived him. He had not cared for himself since the king left. David divided the property between Mefibosjet and Ziba.

keyEvents.title: Spared from the Gibeonites' revenge
keyEvents.description: When the Gibeonites demanded the surrender of Saul's descendants, David spared Mefibosjet because of the oath he had sworn to Jonathan.
